hypotheses.reasoning: The earliest anomaly is catalog-svc failing calls to the third-party translation API (api.translate.example) at 06:10:12Z with HTTP 502, followed by 503 Bad Gateway at 06:10:36Z and 502 at 06:11:18Z. The failures are fast HTTP error responses, not timeouts, which points to the external dependency reporting itself down. catalog-svc's breaker opened at 06:11:57Z (87% failure rate), and it re-opened after a failed half-open probe at 06:24:39Z (#1656), so the outage was still ongoing. Downstream, search-api got 503s from catalog-svc (circuit open) at #1179 and #1542, and web-bff returned GET /search 503s (#1104, #1217, #1598). Those are impact, not cause. Before 06:10 all search and catalog calls were healthy (#1026, #1027), and catalog-db, index-worker and redis-cache show no errors. The analytics-forwarder 429s are a separate, unrelated noise source. A config or credential problem on the translate call would also return error codes, but the logs give no evidence of one, so external_outage is preferred.

If the translation API were hanging rather than failing fast, the calls would show timeouts and the breaker would open on timeouts. The logs show HTTP 502/503 responses instead, so this is a weaker reading of the same lines.

verdict.recommendedAction: Escalate to the translation API provider and confirm their status. Keep catalog-svc's circuit breaker in place so search fails fast instead of piling up. Consider degrading search to skip translation, or serving cached or untranslated results, until the upstream recovers. Check the breaker's half-open probe cadence and restore traffic once it succeeds. Separately, look at analytics-forwarder's 429 retries and drops, which are unrelated to this incident.
